scenario: AITA for asking my pregnant SIL to leave the family Christmas gathering? | Okay so based on title I totally sound like an asshole but hear me out. So this year is our turn to host the family Christmas party at our home. We invited not only my SOs side but also my side as well. Overall it was around 20ish people in our home today for gift giving and typical American Christmas celebrating. Drinks were shared, food broken, the whole shebang. Amongst my SOs side of the family was his pregnant sister. She, I think, was due maybe a week or so ago? But really its just been ticking time bomb for her little one to arrive. Everybodys excited to meet the baby! Now our problem is that SIL came to the party with contractions and was obviously in labor (I know this because Im a mom myself - once you know, you know). Every 20 minutes or so she would start having pains and would make noises to pass the contractions. At first it wasnt so bad; I understand how sucky it is and you dont want to go to the hospital too soon because they'll just send you right home. But then it became almost obnoxious. I feel terrible for saying that but it really was. A lot of my family members and some of hers were glancing around like WTF? Go home and do that in private. After a while it became apparent that it was making everybody uncomfortable and even my MIL reccommend that she rest at home before it gets too late. She refused and said she was fine. In the middle of the kids opening their presents she went into pain again and this time she even screamed for a second. I then discreetly pulled her husband to the side and told them to leave. I did it politely ("Hey I appreciate you guys for being here but I think its time to go. I dont want you guys to give birth in our kitchen! lol"). After I said that her husband got angry and quickly got her and the kids packed up. She visibly upset and before heading out called me a bitch and said that I ruined Christmas for her. A few of their sides family members gave me dirty looks and left soon after. Im torn on this: I wanted everybody to have a good day but it was very distracting and obnoxious to have her around. I feel bad but still. tl;dr -- I asked SIL to leave family Christmas party because she was in labor.

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it's right or wrong for someone to ask their pregnant sister-in-law to leave the family Christmas gathering because she was in labor. From what I understand, the person hosting the party noticed that their sister-in-law was having contractions and it was getting pretty disruptive. They asked her to leave politely, but she got upset and called them a name, and some of her family left too. The person feels bad but also thinks it was distracting and obnoxious to have her around. First, I need to understand the situation better. The family was hosting a Christmas party with around 20 people. It's a time for gift-giving and celebrating. The sister-in-law was due any day, and she came to the party with contractions. At first, it wasn't too bad, but as time went on, it became more disruptive. People were glancing around, and even the mother-in-law suggested she rest at home. When the sister-in-law screamed during a contraction while the kids were opening presents, the host decided to ask them to leave. I think the host's intention was to maintain the atmosphere of the party and ensure that everyone could enjoy themselves. However, asking someone to leave, especially someone who is in labor, seems harsh. On the other hand, the host felt that her presence was making the gathering uncomfortable and distracting for others. I wonder if there were other ways to handle the situation without asking her to leave. Maybe offering her a quiet space to rest or suggesting that she go home to be more comfortable. It might have been better to approach the situation with more empathy and support rather than asking her to leave. Also, considering cultural and social norms, in many families, hosting a party means taking care of all guests, including those who might be in need of special attention. The host might have felt overwhelmed, but perhaps there were other ways to manage the situation. Moreover, the sister-in-law was in labor, which is a sensitive and personal time. She might have felt embarrassed or stressed, which could have contributed to her reaction. The host's decision to ask her to leave might have been seen as unsupportive, especially during such a vulnerable time. In conclusion, while the host's intention was to maintain the party's atmosphere, asking the sister-in-law to leave might have been the wrong approach. It would have been better to offer support and find alternative solutions to accommodate her needs without making her feel excluded or uncomfortable.
